title: Stop double point spends with lockForUpdate
summary: A point spend that goes through twice when the button is mashed gets a transaction and a row lock, and deadlocks get retried.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Services;

use App\Exceptions\InsufficientPointsException;
use App\Models\PointHistory;
use App\Models\User;

class PointService
{
    public function spend(User $user, int $amount, string $reason): void
    {
        if ($user->points < $amount) {
            throw new InsufficientPointsException();
        }

        $user->points -= $amount;
        $user->save();

        PointHistory::create([
            'user_id' => $user->id,
            'amount' => -$amount,
            'reason' => $reason,
        ]);
    }
}

turns.user: user with 100 points spams the 100pt reward button and it goes through twice, balance ends at -100. fix pls. prod is mysql

assistant.body: Great question! Both requests read a balance of 100, both pass the check, and both subtract. $user was loaded at the start of the request, so it knows nothing about the other one.

Let's read the users row again with lockForUpdate() inside DB::transaction. That is SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, so the second request waits until the first one commits. The check, the decrement and the history row become one atomic step.

turns.user: added it, still -100 when i hit it in parallel

assistant.body: Apologies, that was my mistake. The row was locked, but the check still used $user->points, read before the lock. The request that waited sees the old 100 and passes anyway. The check has to use $locked, the row read under the lock.

turns.user: fixed. also when the monthly point grant batch overlaps we get Deadlock found when trying to get lock and a 500. it goes through on retry so dont error

assistant.body: Sure. The second argument to DB::transaction is the number of attempts. On a deadlock or a lock wait timeout it rolls back and runs the closure again from the top. The insufficient points exception is not retried and is thrown as before. Note: inside an outer transaction nothing is retried, and the exception goes straight out.
